Class IteratorAdapterTest

java.lang.Object
myTest.IteratorAdapterTest
public class IteratorAdapterTest extends Object
Test suite for the IteratorAdapter class.

This test suite verifies the functionality of the IteratorAdapter class, which implements the HIterator interface to iterate over elements of a VectorAdapter or SubListAdapter. The tests cover various scenarios including normal iteration, element removal, edge cases, and error conditions.

Test Case Design

The test cases are designed to validate the behavior of IteratorAdapter against the specifications of Java 1.4.2 Iterator interface. The test design includes categories for basic functionality, edge cases, error conditions, and sublist-specific behavior.

Testing Framework Information

This test suite utilizes JUnit 4.13 testing framework with Hamcrest 1.3 matchers for assertions. These dependencies are located as follows:

  • JUnit 4.13: lib/junit-4.13.jar
  • Hamcrest Core 1.3: Matcher/hamcrest-core-1.3.jar

Categories:

  • Basic functionality tests
  • Empty collection tests
  • Null element tests
  • Duplicate element tests
  • Element removal tests
  • SubList iterator tests
  • Nested SubList iterator tests
  • Exception handling tests

    • testHasNextAtTheBeginning

      public void testHasNextAtTheBeginning()
      Test method to verify that hasNext() returns true at the beginning of iteration.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that hasNext() returns true when called at the beginning of iteration on a non-empty collection.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the basic functionality of hasNext() method at the start of iteration. This validates the presence of elements.

      Test Description:

      The test immediately checks if hasNext() returns true, indicating that elements are available for iteration.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HIterator is created from vector.iterator()

      - No next() calls have been made on the iterator

      Post-Condition:

      - hasNext() returns true

      - Iterator position remains unchanged

      Expected Results:

      hasNext() should return true when called at the beginning of iteration on a non-empty collection.

    • testHasNextInTheMiddle

      public void testHasNextInTheMiddle()
      Test method to verify that hasNext() returns true in the middle of iteration.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that hasNext() returns true when called in the middle of iteration.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate hasNext() behavior after partially consuming elements from the iterator. Reporting the presence of remaining elements.

      Test Description:

      The test calls next() three times to advance the iterator position, then checks if hasNext() still returns true, indicating that more elements are available.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HIterator is created from vector.iterator()

      - next() has been called three times

      Post-Condition:

      - hasNext() returns true

      - Iterator position is at the fourth element

      Expected Results:

      hasNext() should return true when called in the middle of iteration with remaining elements.

    • testHasNextAtTheEnd

      public void testHasNextAtTheEnd()
      Test method to verify that hasNext() returns false at the end of iteration.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that hasNext() returns false after all elements have been traversed.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the terminal behavior of hasNext() method. Ensuring it reports when no more elements are available.

      Test Description:

      The test iterates through all elements with hasNext() and next(), then checks if hasNext() returns false after exhaustion.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HIterator is created from vector.iterator()

      - All elements have been consumed by calling next() until hasNext() returns false

      Post-Condition:

      - hasNext() returns false

      - Iterator position is at the end of the collection

      Expected Results:

      hasNext() should return false after all elements have been traversed from the iterator.

    • testNextThrowsException

      public void testNextThrowsException()
      Test method to verify that next() throws NoSuchElementException after iteration completion.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that next() throws NoSuchElementException when called after all elements have been traversed.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate exception handling for the boundary condition of calling next() on an exhausted iterator.

      Test Description:

      The test consumes all elements using next() and hasNext(), then attempts to call next() again, expecting a NoSuchElementException to be thrown.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HIterator is created from vector.iterator()

      - All elements have been traversed by calling next() until hasNext() returns false

      Post-Condition:

      - NoSuchElementException is thrown

      - Iterator remains in exhausted state

      Expected Results:

      next() should throw NoSuchElementException when called on an exhausted iterator.

    • testNextDuplicateElements

      public void testNextDuplicateElements()
      Test method to verify proper iteration over collections with duplicate elements.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that iterators correctly handle collections containing duplicate elements, ensuring proper element retrieval.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate iterator behavior with duplicate values. This ensures that value repetition doesn't affect the iteration process or element counting.

      Test Description:

      The test creates a VectorAdapter with three identical string elements "0". It verifies that next() returns "0" three times in sequence, and that hasNext() returns false after the third element.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 3 elements: ["0", "0", "0"]

      - HIterator is created from vector.iterator()

      Post-Condition:

      - Three elements are returned, all with value "0"

      - hasNext() returns false after the third element

      - Iterator position is at the end of the collection

      Expected Results:

      next() should return all duplicate elements in sequence, and hasNext() should return false after all elements have been traversed.

    • testRemoveAtTheBeginning

      public void testRemoveAtTheBeginning()
      Test method to verify proper element removal at the beginning of iteration.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that remove() correctly removes the first element when called after the first next() call.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate removal functionality at the start of iteration. This ensures that the iterator properly handles structural modifications and integrity when removing the first element.

      Test Description:

      The test immediatly calls next() once to position calls remove() to delete it. The test verifies that the collection size decreases, the first element changes, and the removed element is no longer present.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HIterator is created from vector.iterator()

      - next() has been called once, positioning at the first element

      Post-Condition:

      - Collection size decreases from 5 to 4

      - First element becomes "2" instead of "1"

      - Element "1" is no longer in the collection

      - Iterator position is adjusted accordingly

      Expected Results:

      remove() should successfully delete the first element, decrease collection size, and maintain proper collection structure and iterator position.

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - Element at index 2 becomes null instead of "3"

      - Iterator position is adjusted accordingly

      Expected Results:

      remove() should successfully delete the middle element, decrease collection size, and maintain proper collection structure and iterator position.

      - HIterator is created from vector.iterator()

      - No next() calls have been made

      Post-Condition:

      - Collection remains unchanged

      - Iterator position remains unchanged

      Expected Results:

    • testRemoveThrowsExceptionAfterRemove

      public void testRemoveThrowsExceptionAfterRemove()
      Test method to verify that remove() throws IllegalStateException when called consecutively.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that remove() throws IllegalStateException when called twice without an intervening next() call.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate exception handling for consecutive remove() calls. This ensures that the iterator enforces the proper repositioning and prevents multiple consecutive removals.

      Test Description:

      The test calls next() once to position at the first element, calls remove() to delete it, then immediately attempts to call remove() again without an intervening next() call, expecting an IllegalStateException to be thrown.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HIterator is created from vector.iterator()

      - next() has been called once and remove() has been called once

      Post-Condition:

      - IllegalStateException is thrown on second remove() call

      - Collection contains 4 elements after first removal

      - Iterator position remains after first removal

      Expected Results:

      remove() should throw IllegalStateException when called consecutively without an intervening next() call.
